job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: In 1905, Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal, claiming it was for administrative efficiency due to the province's vast size. However, the real motive was to weaken the growing nationalist movement by dividing the Hindu and Muslim populations. By 1920, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat movement, urging Indians to boycott British institutions. This was not a sign of weakness, but a powerful tool called Satyagraha, which emphasized truth and non-violent resistance rather than passive submission. In 1922, Gandhi abruptly called off this movement after the Chauri Chaura incident turned violent, proving his commitment to non-violence over political gain. Later, in 1930, Gandhi chose salt for his civil disobedience campaign because it was a basic necessity consumed by all, including the poorest, and was unfairly taxed. The movement was not about luxury, but about challenging an unjust monopoly. By 1942, the Quit India movement began, which saw widespread mass participation and spontaneous protests across the country. Unlike earlier movements, this phase witnessed significant public anger and was not merely a quiet protest. Throughout these decades, the Indian National Congress evolved from a group of professionals and intellectuals into a mass movement representing diverse sections of society, eventually facing the complex political pressures that led to the 1947 partition.

items.evidence: However, the real motive was to weaken the growing nationalist movement by dividing the Hindu and Muslim populations.
items.q: Why did Curzon's partition of Bengal anger nationalists, even though it was called an administrative step?
options: It was meant to split and weaken their movement
It was meant to punish farmers for unpaid taxes
It was meant to make the province easier to run
It was meant to end the rule of Bengal's zamindars
items.explain: The real motive was to weaken the nationalist movement by dividing Hindus and Muslims, not just ease administration.

wrong.why: picks a nearby group and blames an unrelated cause
accepts the official claim of administrative ease
invents a political aim not in the passage

items.evidence: This was not a sign of weakness, but a powerful tool called Satyagraha, which emphasized truth and non-violent resistance rather than passive submission.
items.q: How is Satyagraha different from simply accepting British rule quietly?
options: It actively resists injustice while staying non-violent
It resists injustice by using force when needed
It accepts injustice to avoid any trouble
It resists injustice only through speeches and prayers
items.explain: Satyagraha is active, truthful, non-violent resistance, not passive submission.

wrong.why: thinks resisting the British needed violence
narrows resistance to words, ignoring boycott

items.evidence: In 1922, Gandhi abruptly called off this movement after the Chauri Chaura incident turned violent, proving his commitment to non-violence over political gain.
items.q: Gandhi ended the movement just as it was spreading. What does this show about him?
options: He valued non-violence above winning politically
He feared the British would arrest him soon
He believed the movement was already successful
He wanted a separate movement with salt instead
items.explain: He stopped it after Chauri Chaura turned violent, showing he put non-violence above political gain.

wrong.why: thinks Gandhi acted out of fear of arrest
assumes he stopped because the goal was reached
mixes up Non-Cooperation with the later salt campaign

items.evidence: Later, in 1930, Gandhi chose salt for his civil disobedience campaign because it was a basic necessity consumed by all, including the poorest, and was unfairly taxed.
items.q: Why was salt a good choice for a campaign that ordinary Indians would join?
options: Every family used it, so the tax hurt all
Only rich families used it, so the tax was unfair
It was the costliest item the British taxed
Its tax was the only one Indians paid
items.explain: Salt was a basic need of all, even the poorest, so its unfair tax affected everyone.

wrong.why: thinks salt was chosen as a costly luxury
over-generalises one tax into the only tax

items.evidence: Throughout these decades, the Indian National Congress evolved from a group of professionals and intellectuals into a mass movement representing diverse sections of society, eventually facing the complex political pressures that led to the 1947 partition.
items.q: How did the Congress change between its early years and the 1940s?
options: It grew from an elite group into a mass movement
It shrank from a mass movement into an elite group
It began as a party of poor farmers and stayed so
It began as a party demanding Pakistan and later dropped it
items.explain: Congress began as professionals and intellectuals and grew into a mass movement of many sections of society.

wrong.why: thinks Congress was a farmers' party from the start
thinks Pakistan was Congress's plan from the beginning
